title: Projectile range reusing a prior legal but wrong step result
prompt: A projectile is launched at speed v0 = 20 m/s from flat ground at angle θ = 30°. Step 1: note that the identity (v0 cos θ)(v0 sin θ) = (1/2) v0^2 sin(2θ) / 1 is a legal rearrangement used in range derivations. Step 2: someone hands you the intermediate claim that the flight time is t = v0 / g (a formula that is legal for vertical throw-up-and-down to the same height with different bookkeeping). Using that handed flight time with horizontal speed v0 cos θ, report the range. Then recompute the range with the correct flight time 2 v0 sin θ / g and compare.
silentWrongRisk: Step-N result replaced with another legal kinematics formula that is wrong for this flat-ground angled launch claim; the wrong range can still look dimensionally fine.

intendedFailureModes: accepting t = v0/g for angled flat-ground flight
producing a numeric range from the wrong t without flagging it
treating dimensional legality of v0/g as proof for this claim
oracleNotes.referenceApproach: Correct flat-ground time is 2 v0 sinθ / g; range is v0^2 sin(2θ)/g. The handed t = v0/g is a different legal expression reused out of place. No live score.
